stops.stop: Eckernforde, the grave under the storm flood
stops.date_confidence: attested: the gravestone in St. Nicolai was destroyed in the Baltic storm surge of 1872, per literaturland-sh.de, and the Eckernforde city museum states that the grave is no longer findable and that nothing marks it. The 1872 Ostseesturmflut struck on 12-13 November; the day here follows that event and is not separately given by the source. The 2009 hoax is dated 1 April 2009 by the same page.

stops.stop: Mount Shasta, California: the Master on the mountain
stops.date_confidence: religious testimony, not a historical claim; the encounter is dated to August 1930 by the English Wikipedia and narrated in Guy Ballard's Unveiled Mysteries (1934). Steiner's identification of the count with Christian Rosenkreuz is dated 27 September 1911 and was delivered at Neuchatel, not in Germany as the pool's chronology has it; rsarchive.org returned HTTP 403 and the primary lecture text could not be checked. Blavatsky's naming of Master Rakoczi runs from Isis Unveiled (1877) and a Theosophist article of May 1881, and is absent from blavatsky.journey.json.

stops.stop: Troyes, the manuscript that carries his name
stops.date_confidence: the manuscript, MS 2400 in the Troyes library, is late eighteenth century and undated; the attribution rests on a pasted bookseller's note and a pencil note tying it to Cagliostro. The stop date is that of Manly P. Hall's Los Angeles edition, The Most Holy Trinosophia (1933), which carried the attribution into modern circulation; the Dictionary of Gnosis and Western Esotericism calls the text pseudo-Saint-Germain. Month and day defaulted.
stops.sun_caveat: year precision: the Sun could be in any sign; the reading above is for the stated (defaulted or conventional) day and should not be trusted
